newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 GDP may grow 5.7 pct -- stats office.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 GDP may grow 5.7 pct -- stats office.

text.p: Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) is likely to have grown by about 5.7 percent in 1996, Central Statistical Office (GUS) deputy president Roman Sawinski said on Monday.
"Over the year this (GDP) growth may work out at about 5.7 to 5.8 percent," Sawinski told a news conference.

He said GDP had risen by 5.4 percent in the first three quarters of the year but a fall in industrial sales and construction in October and November would probably lead to a slower rate of growth in the final three months. The reason for this slowdown was probably the onset of winter, Sawinski added.
He said that despite the slower fourth quarter, he did not expect any problem in exceeding the 1996 budget estimate of 5.5 percent GDP growth.
Earlier on Monday, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said he expected Poland to register GDP growth of 6.7 to 7.0 percent for 1996.
